memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The Lord said to Abram after Lot had parted from him, "Look around from where you are, to the north and south, to the east and west. All the land that you see I will give to you and your offspring forever." - Gen 13:14-15 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The timing here is everything: God speaks "after Lot had parted from him." Abram had just let go of the best land, watched his nephew walk away, and been left with the leftovers. And in that moment of apparent loss, God shows up with a promise bigger than anything Lot took.

Notice the gentle echo. Lot "looked around and saw" the well-watered plain and grabbed it for himself (v.10). Now God says to Abram, "Look around from where you are... All the land that you see I will give to you." Lot looked and took. Abram looked and received. What Lot seized, God gave.

There is such comfort here for anyone who has lost out by doing the right thing. Abram's generosity looked like foolishness - he gave away the good land. But you cannot out-give God. What Abram surrendered for peace, God returned to him multiplied.

This particular land promise was made to Abram and his offspring, not transferred to us. But the character of God shines through it unchanged: He is a God who sees sacrifice and honours it, who meets us in our losses with His promises. Jesus said it plainly: "no one who has left home or... fields for me and the gospel will fail to receive a hundred times as much" (Mark 10:29-30). Let go in faith. God is not slow to fill empty hands.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Have you lost something by choosing to do what was right?
- Can you trust God to meet you in your losses?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You that You see every sacrifice and meet me in my losses. When I let go for the sake of peace or obedience, help me trust that Your promises are greater than anything I release.
Amen.
